metadata.note: Yes -- West Seneca, NY (specifically its Gardenville and Ebenezer hamlets) had electric interurban rail service, via two separate lines both operated under the Erie County Traction Company umbrella: the Buffalo, Gardenville and Ebenezer Railway (BG&E) and the Buffalo, Hamburg and Aurora Railway (BH&A, which despite its name only ever reached Orchard Park, not Hamburg or East Aurora). Both were part of the broader wave of Buffalo-area interurban lines (alongside the International Railway Company's city and suburban network) that flourished in the early 1900s and were abandoned in the 1930s as buses took over. GEOMETRY LIMITATION: real-traced OpenStreetMap track geometry could not be attempted for these lines -- the Overpass API was unreachable (connection refused / internal server error on both the primary endpoint and the kumi.systems mirror) at the time this was researched. Geometry shown here is a straight-line approximation between the real, correctly-ordered, geocoded town/hamlet locations (Buffalo, Gardenville, Ebenezer, Orchard Park) -- flagged honestly rather than presented as traced track. Should be upgraded to real track geometry (checking for abandoned/disused rail tagging) once the Overpass service is reachable again.
sources: https://cptdb.ca/wiki/index.php/International_Railway_Company_(NY/ON) (International Railway Company formed 1902 merger of Buffalo-area interurban/street railways; discontinued all interurban rail service in 1937, remaining streetcars ended July 1 1950)

properties.line: Buffalo, Gardenville and Ebenezer: Buffalo – Ebenezer

segments.note: The Buffalo, Gardenville and Ebenezer Railway (BG&E), part of the Erie County Traction Company, ran an electric interurban from Buffalo south through the Gardenville and Ebenezer hamlets of West Seneca. Exact opening date not found in available sources (estimated to the general 1895-1905 Erie County Traction expansion era, alongside the 1900-opened Buffalo, Hamburg and Aurora line); abandoned in 1937 along with the rest of the region's interurban network. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

properties.line: Buffalo, Hamburg and Aurora: Buffalo – Orchard Park

segments.note: The Buffalo, Hamburg and Aurora Railway (BH&A), part of the Erie County Traction Company, opened in 1900 as an electric interurban running south from Buffalo through West Seneca to Orchard Park; despite the name, it never reached its intended destination of East Aurora. Abandoned in 1932, when buses replaced the trolleys. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
